_comment: How each place of the catalogue's words-02.jsonl was settled before it went in config/figures-seen/: two readers read every place against its BSB verse, one asking whether the figure is plainly there and one whether the marked words, form and tags are right; a place both passed is kept as handed over, and any place either questioned was read a third time and kept, changed or dropped. A new form stands only where a reader proposed it. Places not read are held, not listed.

Then kept figures of speech were read again by two readers, a third settling any difference ("words re-read" counts them: those a sample showed at risk, such as wide spans, or those found only in the Hebrew or Greek that carry no tags): each kept as it was, cut to the words that carry the figure, or dropped ("words").

Then every kept place that marks three or more poetry lines as said twice, opposite, building or climbing was read again by two readers, a third settling any difference: each kept all its lines, kept only the lines that stand in the relation, or was dropped ("span").

Last, a sample of 25 kept places was read by two more readers, a third settling any split; the file goes in only when 24 or more pass, and any place that fails is dropped. "samples" lists each sample and its result.

Strong's tags are also taken off any kept place whose tags light the article (G3588) or the object marker (H0853), or number eight, the search's limit, or whose roots light more words of the verse than there are tags, or, on a question or parallel lines, that were chosen for marked words since changed: such tags are a stretch of words, or name words no longer marked.

places.why: The restating ("You conceive chaff; you give birth to stubble") sits inside one BSB line, so no line says another again. Line 2, "Your breath is a fire that will consume you", carries the picture on in a different shape and is not a plain parallel line.

places.span_why: The verse holds two pairs. The fear in "The sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling grips the ungodly" is not restated by their cry, which is a separate pair. The fear lines are the cleanest restatement: sinners become the ungodly, and afraid becomes trembling. The cry moves from "consuming fire" up to "everlasting flames", so it rises rather than only restating.

places.why: Line 3, "Where is he who counts the towers?", plainly asks line 2's question again. Line 1, "Your mind will ponder the former terror", only introduces them, so it comes out of the span.

"Look upon Zion" is plainly said again as "Your eyes will see Jerusalem", and "its tent pegs will not be pulled up, / nor will any of its cords be broken" is a second restating pair. Both are plain in the BSB. The tags mark "city of" and "appointed feast", which pair with nothing, and they miss the first verb "look" (H2372).
places.span_why: "the city of our appointed feasts" and "a peaceful pasture, a tent that does not wander" add new pictures, so not all six lines restate each other. "its tent pegs will not be pulled up, / nor will any of its cords be broken" is a plain restatement.
"angry with all the nations / furious with all their armies" is one pair. "He will devote them to destruction" is a second pair about what He will do, not a restatement of His anger.
The falling oxen and bulls and the drenched land are two separate pairs. "Their land will be drenched with blood, / and their soil will be soaked with fat" is the clearest restatement.

The overgrown towers and "a haunt for jackals, an abode for ostriches" are two different pictures. "Her towers will be overgrown with thorns, / her fortresses with thistles and briers" restates plainly.

"He has allotted their portion" is about God's giving, and "They will possess it forever" is about their keeping it, so they are two pairs. The second pair restates most plainly: "possess it forever" is said again as "dwell in it from generation to generation". The first pair adds "His hand" and "by measure".

places.why: "No lion will be there, / and no vicious beast will go up on it" plainly says one thing twice. Line 4, "but the redeemed will walk upon it", sets an opposite, so the span ends at the first pair.

"Whom have you taunted and blasphemed?" is plainly asked again in "Against whom have you raised your voice and lifted your eyes in pride?" Line 4, "Against the Holy One of Israel!", answers the question and comes out of the span.

"a remnant will go forth from Jerusalem, / and survivors from Mount Zion" plainly restate each other, and the tags (remnant/survivors, Jerusalem/Mount Zion, go out) point at them. "The zeal of the LORD of Hosts / will accomplish this" is one sentence split over two lines and comes out of the span.

"He will go back the way he came" and "he will not enter this city" name two linked outcomes, but it is not plain that the second says the first again. Line 3 is the speech formula "declares the LORD". Not plain enough for an unsourced mark.

The two pairs run plainly parallel ("I will never again see the LORD ... in the land of the living" / "I will no longer look on mankind with those who dwell in this world"). The second pair adds mankind to the LORD, so it adds to the first rather than saying it again: Built on, not Said twice.

"I chirp like a swallow or crane; / I moan like a dove" plainly say one thing twice. "My eyes grow weak as I look upward" and "O Lord, I am oppressed; be my security" are new thoughts and come out of the span.

No line says another again. "What can I say?" is a question, "He has spoken to me, and He Himself has done this" answers it, and "I will walk slowly all my years / because of the anguish of my soul" is one sentence over two lines.

"I had such great anguish; / but Your love has delivered me" tells of a turn from distress to rescue, not two parallel lines opposed in sense. "for You have cast all my sins behind Your back" gives a reason, not an opposite.

The address lines do say the same thing again: "O Zion, herald of good news" and "O Jerusalem, herald of good news." The commands do not. "Go up on a high mountain" and "Raise your voice loudly" are two different acts, climbing and then shouting, and the next line goes further still ("Lift it up"). So the second pair adds to the first instead of restating it. That is building or alternating lines, not plainly "same", and in doubt it fails.

"He tends His flock like a shepherd" is filled out by different acts ("gathers the lambs ... carries them ... gently leads the nursing ewes"), not said again. These are a run of description, not plainly paired lines.

"No sooner are they planted, no sooner are they sown, / no sooner have their stems taken root" says "barely begun" twice over. "He blows on them and they wither, / and a whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble" says their end twice. Each pair plainly restates.
places.span_why: "than He blows on them and they wither" finishes the sentence with the opposite outcome. It does not restate the planting. The "no sooner" lines restate each other.

places.why: "He leads forth the starry host by number; / He calls each one by name" plainly restate each other. The command and question in lines 1 and 2 and the cause in lines 5 and 6 are not restating pairs, so they come out of the span.

places.span_why: The question and the quoted complaint "My way is hidden from the LORD" are two separate pairs. "Why do you say, O Jacob, / and why do you assert, O Israel" is a plain restatement: say becomes assert, and Jacob becomes Israel. The tags (Jacob, declare, Israel) sit on these lines, so keeping them keeps the tags right.

places.why: "Let them come forward and testify; / let us together draw near for judgment" plainly say one thing twice. "Be silent before Me" and "renew their strength" are two different commands, so lines 1 and 2 come out of the span.
"The islands see and fear; / the ends of the earth tremble" plainly restate each other. Line 3, "They approach and come forward", adds a new action and comes out of the span.

No line sets an opposite: the only "but" is inside line 1. The verse is two plainly restating pairs ("seek water, but there is none; / their tongues are parched with thirst" and "I, the LORD, will answer them; / I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them"), so it is Said twice.
places.span_why: "I, the LORD, will answer them" answers the need in "The poor and needy seek water". It does not restate it. The clearest pair is "I, the LORD, will answer them; / I, the God of Israel, will not forsake them."

Lines 1 to 4 are one question carried across purpose clauses, and "so that we may say: 'He was right'" goes past "so that we may know". The answer that follows is a separate thought. "No one announced it, no one foretold it, / no one heard your words" plainly says the same denial again.

"But now I will groan like a woman in labor" sets the opposite against the silence, and an opposite cannot stand in a "same" place. "I have kept silent ... / I have remained quiet and restrained" restates plainly.

places.why: "I will lead the blind ... / I will guide them on unfamiliar paths" and "darkness into light ... / rough places into level ground" plainly restate. "These things I will do for them, / and I will not forsake them" sums up and adds a promise, so it comes out of the span.
places.span_why: "I will turn darkness into light ... and rough places into level ground" is a new picture. The clear restatement is "lead the blind by a way they did not know / guide them on unfamiliar paths".

places.why: Nothing is set against its opposite ("but" means "except"). "Who is blind but My servant, / or deaf like the messenger ... / Who is blind like My covenant partner, / or blind like the servant of the LORD?" plainly asks one thing four times, so it is Said twice.

"Who among you will pay attention to this? / Who will listen and obey hereafter?" plainly asks the same thing twice. The one tag, H0238 "give ear", is one of the paired verbs, so it points at the figure even though it does not show both halves.

"They were unwilling to walk in His ways, / and they would not obey His law" (the pair the search found) plainly restate each other. "Was it not the LORD, / against whom we have sinned?" is one question over two lines and does not belong in the span.

The "but" marks their dullness, not an opposite line. "It enveloped them in flames, / but they did not understand" is plainly said again as "it consumed them, / but they did not take it to heart", so it is Said twice over those four lines. The opening line about the poured-out anger comes out of the span.

places.span_why: "When you walk through the fire" brings a new picture after the waters, so the place mixes two pictures. In the water lines, "I will be with you" and "they will not overwhelm you" are different promises, not a restatement. "you will not be scorched; / the flames will not set you ablaze" is the plain restatement.
"Because you are precious ... and because I love you" gives the reason and does not restate what follows. "I will give men in exchange for you / and nations in place of your life" restates plainly.

places.why: In the BSB, line 2 gives the reason for line 1 ("you have not called on Me, O Jacob, / because you have grown weary of Me, O Israel"), so it is one sentence over two lines, not a restatement. The tags mark the conjunction "for" (H3588A), which carries no figure.

places.span_why: The Spirit pair turns from the picture of the land to the people, which is a new thought, so all four lines are not one restatement. "pour water on the thirsty land, / and currents on the dry ground" restates most exactly: water becomes currents, and thirsty land becomes dry ground.

places.why: Only lines 5-6 restate: "the things to come" / "what is to take place". Line 1 is a question and line 4 is a reason, so the mark is narrowed to lines 5-6.

The lines are the craftsman's successive steps (measuring line, stylus, chisels, compass, fashioning). Each one adds a new act and none restates the one before. Calling a plain list of acts "building" would not show a figure plainly.
The verse is a narrative sequence: burns half, roasts meat, eats, warms himself and speaks. No line restates another.
The lines go step by step from making the god to bowing, praying and the words of the prayer. That is progression, not a restatement, and not a plain figure.

"no one considers in his heart" / "no one has the knowledge or insight" plainly restate. Lines 3-5 are a narrative list, and in lines 6-7 making and bowing down are different acts, so only lines 1-2 are marked.

The four lines are a command, a reason, a creation claim and a promise. Line 3 repeats "you are My servant" but adds "I have made you", and the verse's shape (remember ... never forget) is not plainly "said twice". The tags fall on names and on "for", not on any figure.
"break down the gates of bronze" / "cut through the bars of iron" plainly restate. "I will go before you / and level the mountains" adds a second act, so only lines 3-4 are marked.
Raising Cyrus, making his ways straight, rebuilding the city, freeing the exiles, then a qualifier and a speech formula: these are successive acts, and no line restates another.
The eight lines mix a speech formula, a run of creation verbs, a not/but pair and God's claim. No single relation holds across them, and no pair is plainly "said twice".
"Who foretold this long ago? / Who announced it from ancient times?" plainly restate. The summons and the closing claims are not restatements, so only lines 3-4 are marked.

places.span_why: "By Myself I have sworn ... a word that will not be revoked" introduces the oath, and "Every knee will bow" is what is sworn. The clearest pair is "Every knee will bow before Me, / every tongue will swear allegiance."

places.why: "unable to relieve the burden; / but they themselves go into captivity" does not set an opposite. It goes a step further in the same direction, and line 1 takes no part, so no live form is plain here.

places.span_why: "I have made you" and "deliver you" bring in new thoughts. "Even to your old age" is said again as "when you turn gray" in the first pair.

places.why: "pour out their bags of gold / and weigh out silver on scales" plainly restate. Hiring the goldsmith and bowing down move the action on, so only lines 1-2 are marked.
"there it stands" / "not budging from that spot" (its place = that spot) plainly restate. Lifting, carrying, crying out and not saving are a sequence, so only lines 3-4 are marked.
"a bird of prey from the east" / "a man for My purpose from a far-off land" plainly restate. Lines 3-6 go word then deed rather than line-by-line restatement, so only lines 1-2 are marked.

places.span_why: "I will take vengeance; I will spare no one" is God's own act, a separate pair. "Your nakedness will be uncovered / and your shame will be exposed" restates plainly.

places.why: The lines move from God's anger to handing the people over, then to Babylon's lack of mercy and the yoke on the elderly. Each line adds something and none restates the last.

Line 2 does not restate line 1, but the verse plainly alternates: a line on her false security, then "you said, 'No one sees me'", then a line on her wisdom leading her astray, then "you told yourself, 'I am...'". That is A B A' B'.
"Perhaps you will succeed; / perhaps you will inspire terror!" plainly restate. Lines 3-4 are one relative clause split in two, so only lines 5-6 are marked.

"who swear by the name of the LORD, / who invoke the God of Israel" restate each other in the BSB itself. Line 6 sets a contrast and line 3 adds something new. The tags fall on Jacob, Judah, "waters" and so on, and miss LORD, God and "invoke", so they are stripped.

places.span_why: "For I knew how deceitful you are" gives a reason and a new thought. "You have never heard ... / your ears have not been open" restates plainly.

places.why: "For the sake of My name I will delay My wrath; / for the sake of My praise I will restrain it" plainly restate. Line 3 gives the purpose and is not marked.
The "but not" falls inside line 1. Line 2 ("I have tested you in the furnace of affliction") restates "I have refined you" rather than opposing it, so the place is "same", not "opposite".
The lines do not restate each other, but line 1 plainly doubles its phrase for force: "For My own sake, My very own sake". The mark moves to those words, under "doubling".

"Listen to Me, O Jacob, / and Israel, whom I have called" is one address split over two lines. "I am the first, / and I am the last" pairs opposite ends and does not restate. No live form is plain at these words.
"I have not spoken in secret" and "from the time it happened, I was there" make different claims, and the verse then changes speaker. Nothing is said twice.

places.span_why: "their name would never be cut off" is about lasting, not number, so it is a separate pair. "countless as the sand / numerous as its grains" restates plainly.

places.why: "He made water flow for them from the rock; / He split the rock, and water gushed out" plainly restate. Line 1 sets the scene and is not marked.

Line 2 does not restate line 1. The lines plainly alternate: "He made My mouth like a sharp sword" / "He hid Me in the shadow of His hand" / "He made Me like a polished arrow" / "He hid Me in His quiver". That is A B A' B'.

"to raise up the tribes of Jacob, / and to restore the protected ones of Israel" plainly says the same thing twice: tribes of Jacob and protected ones of Israel, raise up and restore. You can see it in the BSB itself. Lines 1, 4 and 5 ("not enough" and "a light for the nations") do not restate it. The tags cover Jacob, preserved and Israel but not "tribes" or the two verbs, so they do not carry the pair.

"Your builders hasten back; / your destroyers and wreckers depart from you" sets builders against destroyers and coming back against going away. The lines are set as opposites, so this is opposite lines, not a restatement. The marked lines are right.

"you will wear them all as jewelry / and put them on like a bride" plainly restates: wear them / put them on, jewelry / like a bride. Lines 1 to 3 ("Lift up your eyes", "They all gather together", "As surely as I live") do not restate one another, so only lines 4 and 5 are marked.

"I was bereaved and barren; / I was exiled and rejected" is a plain pair of lines on her desolation. But exile and rejection are new griefs, not other words for losing her children, so the second line adds to the first (building) rather than saying it again. The questions around the pair ("Who has begotten these for me?", "So who has reared them?") are not part of it.

places.span_why: The eight lines hold several separate pairs (no one answering, God's strength, the dried sea, the dying fish). The clearest is "Is My hand too short to redeem you? / Or do I lack the strength to deliver you?"

places.why: The six lines are not one restating group: the second question adds a new case to the first, and lines 5 and 6 answer them. "Let him trust in the name of the LORD; / let him lean on his God" is the plainest restatement (trust / lean, the name of the LORD / his God), so only those two lines are marked.

"Pay attention to Me, My people, / and listen to Me, My nation" plainly restates in the BSB itself: pay attention / listen, My people / My nation. Line 5 ("I will bring it about quickly") restates nothing, so the five-line span is wrong. The single tag, on "give ear" (H0238), marks only one side of the pair.

The lines alternate A B A' B': "Among all the sons she bore" and "among all the sons she brought up" match, and so do "there is no one to guide her" and "there is no one to take her hand". Line 2 does not restate line 1, so this is alternating lines, not said twice. The marked four lines are right.

Line 2 does not oppose line 1, since the "but not" is inside line 2. The plain figure is "drunken, but not with wine": the verse itself says the drunkenness is not from wine. The verses on either side name the cup of His fury that makes her stagger. She is called drunken for what is only like drunkenness, which is a metaphor. Mark those words only.
places.words_why: "you afflicted one, drunken, but not with wine": the verse itself says this drunkenness is not from wine, so calling the afflicted one "drunken" is plainly a figure (the "cup of staggering" follows in 51:22). The word that carries it is "drunken". "but not with wine" only qualifies it, and the rule is to mark fewer when in doubt.

places.why: "Rise up and sit on your throne" adds a picture nothing else restates. "O captive Daughter of Zion" only names the one addressed. "Shake off your dust!" and "Remove the chains from your neck" are different pictures, so no two lines plainly say the same thing.

"Therefore My people will know My name" is said again as "therefore they will know on that day that I am He who speaks", with "therefore ... know" repeated. "Here I am!" is a separate cry and not part of the pair, so the span is lines 1-3.

places.span_why: "the punishment that brought us peace ... by His stripes we are healed" adds the benefit to us, a new thought. "pierced for our transgressions / crushed for our iniquities" restates plainly.

places.why: "We all like sheep have gone astray, / each one has turned to his own way" plainly restate each other. "and the LORD has laid upon Him / the iniquity of us all" is one clause that answers them, so the span is lines 1-2.
"For My thoughts are not your thoughts, / neither are your ways My ways" plainly say one thing twice. "declares the LORD" is the speech formula, so the span is lines 1-2.

"so My ways are higher than your ways / and My thoughts than your thoughts" restate each other. Line 1, "as the heavens are higher than the earth", is the comparison they answer, not a restating line, so the span is lines 2-3.

No line sets an opposite against another. "will not return to Me empty, but..." says one thing first negatively, then positively. "it will accomplish what I please, / and it will prosper where I send it" plainly say it twice, so the form is "same" on lines 3-4.

"they all turn to their own way, / each one seeking his own gain" plainly restate each other (all // each one, own way // own gain). The earlier lines are a likeness and a new charge, so the span is lines 4-5.

"You have sent your envoys a great distance; / you have descended even to Sheol itself": the second line plainly goes further ("even ... itself"), so it builds rather than says the first line again. Lines 1-2 are one act continued with "and". Keep it as "building" on lines 3-4.

"You are wearied by your many journeys, but you did not say, 'There is no hope!'" is a concession inside one thought, and "You found renewal of your strength; therefore you did not grow weak" is cause and result. No line answers another with its opposite, and no other form is plain. The search keyed on "but".

"I have seen his ways, but I will heal him" is mercy despite sin, and the reader needs 57:17 to see that the ways were sinful. "I will guide him and restore comfort / to him and his mourners" goes on with the promise. These are not plain opposite lines.

places.span_why: "For day after day they seek Me / and delight to know My ways" plainly says one thing twice. "like a nation that does what is right..." adds a comparison, and the last pair stands apart from the first, so I kept only the clearest pair, which also keeps fewer lines.

places.why: "Why have we fasted, / and You have not seen? / Why have we humbled ourselves, / and You have not noticed?" plainly asks one question twice. Lines 5-6 are God's answer in another voice, so the span is lines 1-4.

places.span_why: "rebuild the ancient ruins" / "restore the age-old foundations" restate each other. "you will be called Repairer of the Breach" adds a new thought, the name given, with new pictures.

There are two pairs about different things: bloodstained "hands" and "fingers" (deeds), then "lips" and "tongue" (speech). The clearest pair is "your lips have spoken lies, / and your tongue mutters injustice."

places.why: "No one calls for justice; / no one pleads his case honestly" plainly restate each other. Line 4's new image (conceive / give birth) does not plainly say line 3 again, so the clear span is lines 1-2.

places.span_why: The verse has two separate pairs: the useless "cobwebs" and the wicked "deeds". The plainest is "Their deeds are sinful deeds, / and acts of violence are in their hands" (deeds and acts, sinful and violence), which needs no picture worked out.

places.why: The "but" falls inside each line, and no line opposes another. "We hope for justice, but find none, / for salvation, but it is far from us" plainly says one thing twice (justice // salvation, find none // far from us), so the form is "same" on lines 3-4.

places.span_why: "He saw that there was no man; / He was amazed that there was no one to intercede" restate each other. "So His own arm brought salvation" gives the result, a new thought.

"righteousness like a breastplate" and "the helmet of salvation" are armor that saves, while "garments of vengeance" and "a cloak of zeal" are about punishing. The pair that plainly restates is "He put on garments of vengeance / and wrapped Himself in a cloak of zeal."

places.why: "your sons will come from afar, / and your daughters will be carried on the arm" plainly restate each other. "Lift up your eyes and look around" is a command and "They all gather and come to you" is the general line the pair fills out, so the span is lines 3-4.
"You will drink the milk of nations / and nurse at the breasts of royalty" plainly restate each other. Lines 3-4 are one sentence of titles, not a restatement, so the span is lines 1-2.
"Your sun will no longer set, / and your moon will not wane" plainly restate each other. Lines 3-4 give the reason and add the end of sorrow, so the span is lines 1-2.

Only "they are the branch of My planting, / the work of My hands" plainly say one thing twice. "will be righteous" and "will possess the land forever" are different promises, and "so that I may be glorified" is the purpose, so the span is lines 3-4.

places.span_why: "called the priests of the LORD" / "speak of you as ministers of our God" restate each other. "you will feed on the wealth of nations" is a new thought.

places.why: "Their descendants will be known among the nations, / and their offspring among the peoples" plainly restate each other. Lines 3-4 are one sentence that adds something rather than repeating, so the span is lines 1-2.

places.span_why: "No longer will you be called Forsaken, / nor your land named Desolate; / but you will be called Hephzibah, / and your land Beulah" sets the old names against the new ones. "for the LORD will take delight in you" gives the reason and is not itself an opposite line.

places.why: "Who is this coming from Edom, / from Bozrah with crimson-stained garments?" is asked again as "Who is this robed in splendor, / marching in the greatness of His strength?" (Edom // Bozrah, garments // robed). Lines 5-6 are the answer, so the span is lines 1-4.

These are not opposite lines: the "but" is inside line 1, and "So" joins two couplets as a result. "I looked, but there was no one to help; / I was appalled that no one assisted" plainly says one thing twice, so the form is "same" on lines 1-2.

The six lines are not one restatement. The two "Where is" questions name different acts. What plainly says one thing twice is "remembered the days of old, / the days of Moses", so the span is lines 1-2.

The lines do not say one thing twice. Lines 3-4 give a purpose and its result. What is plain is the likeness with "as": God's coming down (64:1) is compared to "as fire kindles the brushwood and causes the water to boil".

"no one has heard, / no ear has perceived, / no eye has seen any God besides You" plainly says it three times in the English. Line 4 is not part of it, so the span is lines 1-3. The single tag H0238 marks one word of the set, and the figure does not show only in the original.

places.span_why: "You are our Father" is a different picture from the potter. "we are the clay, and You are the potter; / we are all the work of Your hand" plainly restate each other.

places.why: "Do not be angry, O LORD, beyond measure; / do not remember our iniquity forever" plainly restate each other. "Oh, look upon us, we pray; / we are all Your people!" is a new plea with its reason, so the span is lines 1-2.

Nothing opposite is set against anything: "I will not keep silent, but I will repay" says one thing negatively, then positively. "I will pay it back into their laps" plainly says "I will repay" again. "Behold, it is written before Me" only opens the verse, so the form is "same" on lines 2-3.

places.span_why: "descendants from Jacob, / and heirs from Judah" says the same thing twice under one verb. "My elect will possess My mountains, / and My servants will dwell there" is a separate pair about the land, so only the clearest pair is kept.

The opposite is "You will leave behind your name / as a curse" against "but to His servants He will give another name." The line between, "the Lord GOD will slay you", adds a separate thought and is not that opposite.

places.why: "Whoever invokes a blessing in the land will do so by the God of truth" is plainly said again in "whoever takes an oath in the land will swear by the God of truth". Lines 5-6 ("For the former troubles will be forgotten") start a new thought, so the span is lines 1-4.

"No longer will they build houses for others to inhabit, nor plant for others to eat" says one thing twice. The tree likeness and "My chosen ones will fully enjoy" do not restate it, so the span is lines 1-2.

"but the food of the serpent will be dust" is not plainly set against the lines before it as an opposite. The search only caught ", but". What the verse plainly shows is lines 1-2 saying one thing twice: "The wolf and the lamb will feed together" / "the lion will eat straw like the ox" (the beast of prey now at peace). So the place stays as said twice on lines 1-2.

Line 1 does not restate anything. It sets up a likeness, "As a mother comforts her son, so will I comfort you", and that likeness with "as ... so" is the plain figure. Whether line 3 restates line 2 is less clear, because it adds "over Jerusalem".

"the hand of the LORD will be revealed to His servants, but His wrath will be shown to His enemies" plainly sets servants against enemies. Lines 1-2 ("When you see, you will rejoice... like grass") take no part in it.

No line restates the one before. "for He is the Maker of all things" gives a reason, and "Israel is the tribe of His inheritance" turns the relation around. The tags (Jacob, for, formed, all, he, Israel) carry no figure.
"for the LORD has spoken" gives a reason and does not restate "Listen and give heed. Do not be arrogant". The one tag, on "give ear", is a single word inside line 1, not a parallel line.

"O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid ... and do not be dismayed, O Israel" plainly says it twice, and you can see that in the BSB itself. "declares the LORD" breaks into the pair and lines 5-8 are new, so only lines 1, 3 and 4 are marked. The tags take in "declares the LORD" and the later "Jacob" but leave out "fear", so they are dropped.

"But you, O Jacob My servant, do not be afraid, and do not be dismayed, O Israel" plainly says the same thing twice in the BSB. Lines 3-6 do not belong to the pair. The tags miss "fear" and catch the "Jacob" of line 5, so they are dropped.

"May the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon," says the dweller of Zion, is restated by "May my blood be on the dwellers of Chaldea," says Jerusalem. The pairs match: violence and blood, Babylon and Chaldea, Zion and Jerusalem. This is plain in the BSB and both halves are rightly marked. The tags leave out "violence", "flesh" and "Babylon" and take in the preposition "to", so they are dropped.
places.span_why: "May the violence done to me and to my flesh be upon Babylon" is said again as "May my blood be on the dwellers of Chaldea". The speech formulas "says the dweller of Zion" and "says Jerusalem" are left out, as the rule asks, which also keeps fewer lines.

places.why: "Her foes have become her masters; her enemies are at ease" says it twice. Lines 3-6 ("For the LORD has brought her grief", "Her children have gone away") are new statements.

"Zion stretches out her hands, but there is no one to comfort her" is a plea that gets no answer. It is not a line set against its opposite, and the search only caught ", but". The tags spread over Zion, hands, commanded, Yahweh and Jacob, which carry no figure.
"I called out to my lovers, but they have betrayed me" tells of a call met with betrayal. It is not two lines opposed in sense, and lines 3-6 stand in no such relation.

"People have heard my groaning, but there is no one to comfort me" is a lament with no reply, not an opposite line. The rest of the verse sets no opposite either. The place was caught on a mechanical ", but".

"cut off every horn of Israel", "withdrawn His right hand" and "burned in Jacob like a flaming fire" are three different acts. None restates another. The tags fall on names, verbs and prepositions and mark no figure.
"The Lord has rejected His altar; He has abandoned His sanctuary" plainly says it twice. The palace walls and the shout "as on the day of an appointed feast" are new thoughts.

The elders "sit on the ground in silence", throw dust and put on sackcloth, and "The young women of Jerusalem have bowed their heads". These are different mourning acts by different groups, not one line restated. The tags carry no figure.

"To what can I compare you, O Daughter of Jerusalem? To what can I liken you ... O Virgin Daughter of Zion?" is a plain restatement. Lines 7-8 ("your wound is as deep as the sea. Who can ever heal you?") are new, and line 1 is a separate question. The tags miss the verb behind "compare" (H1819) and take in "console", so they are dropped.
places.span_why: "To what can I compare you, / O Daughter of Jerusalem?" is restated as "To what can I liken you, ... / O Virgin Daughter of Zion?". The line "that I may console you" adds a purpose, a new thought.

places.why: "The LORD has done what He planned; He has accomplished His decree, which He ordained in days of old" says it twice. "He has overthrown you without pity" and the lines about the enemy are separate thoughts, so the span is lines 1-3.
places.span_why: "The LORD has done what He planned; / He has accomplished His decree" restate each other. "which He ordained in days of old" is a relative clause that completes the sentence without restating it.

places.why: Nothing is said twice: women eating their offspring and priests killed in the sanctuary are two different horrors. But "Should women eat their offspring...?" and "Should priests and prophets be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?" plainly ask for no answer. They protest to the LORD, who is told "Look ... and consider". So the place stays as a question that is not asking, on those two questions.

"You have slain them in the day of Your anger; You have slaughtered them without compassion" plainly says it twice. Lines 1-4, about the young and old in the dust and those fallen by the sword, are a different thought.

"He left me without help" gives the outcome of "He forced me off my path and tore me to pieces" and does not restate it. Calling it "built on" would only describe two lines in a row, not a figure the words plainly show, so it does not go live.
"You have killed without pity" goes a step past "covered Yourself in anger and pursued us", so it adds rather than restates. It is not plain enough to go live under another form either.
"You said, 'Do not be afraid'" tells what God said after "You drew near when I called on You". It is a next step in the account, not a restatement and not a plain figure.

places.span_why: "Even jackals offer their breasts / to nurse their young, / but the daughter of my people has become cruel" sets nursing against cruelty. "like an ostrich in the wilderness" adds a new picture, a simile, rather than standing as an opposite line.

places.why: "The nursing infant's tongue / clings in thirst" (thirst) and "Little children beg for bread, / but no one gives them any" (hunger, with the new thought that no one gives) do not plainly say the same thing again. No two lines inside either sentence restate each other.

"brighter than snow, / whiter than milk" plainly says the same thing twice. Lines 3 and 4 move to red skin and a blue gem, so they do not restate the white of lines 1 and 2, and they restate each other only loosely. The span is cut to lines 1 and 2.

"The LORD has exhausted His wrath; / He has poured out His fierce anger" plainly says it twice. The fire kindled in Zion that consumes her foundations is a new act, so the span is cut to lines 1 and 2.

"The priests are shown no honor; / the elders find no favor" plainly restates itself, with priests matching elders and honor matching favor. Lines 1 and 2 (scattered them, regards them no more) are a separate thought that does not restate, so the span is cut to lines 3 and 4.

"Our end drew near, our time ran out, / for our end had come!" plainly says the same thing again. Lines 1 and 2 are a cause and its result (stalked, so we could not walk) and do not restate, so the span is cut to lines 3 and 4.

"we are weary and find no rest" does not restate "We are closely pursued", so the place is not "said twice". The second line plainly completes the first by giving what the pursuit leads to. These are the BSB's two poetry lines, so the place is kept as Built on.

"Our fathers sinned and are no more, / but we bear their punishment" does set "fathers" against "we" with "but". Still, line 2 does not state the opposite of line 1. It completes it: "their punishment" cannot stand without line 1, and sin and its punishment are cause and effect, not opposites. "Building" fits at least as well, so the verse does not plainly show "opposite", and with that doubt the place fails.
"I will make her like a desert / and turn her into a parched land" plainly says the same thing twice. Line 5 ("and I will let her die of thirst") adds a new step, so the mark is cut to lines 3-4.

"She will pursue her lovers but not catch them; / she will seek them but not find them" plainly says the same thing twice: pursue/seek, not catch/not find. The "but" sits inside each line, so nothing is set against its opposite. Lines 3-5 are her later resolve and are not part of the pair.
"Do not journey to Gilgal, / do not go up to Beth-aven" plainly restate each other. Lines 1-2 set Israel against Judah and line 5 adds a new command, so the mark is cut to lines 3-4.

"Hear this, O priests! / Take heed, O house of Israel! / Give ear, O royal house!" plainly says the same call three times, and it shows in the BSB itself. The mark is cut to lines 1-3. The lone tag on "give ear" (H0238) does not carry the figure, so it is dropped.

"The rebels are deep in slaughter; / but I will chastise them all": the second line is God's answer to the sin, not its opposite. The search caught only the word "but". Calling it "built on" would be too loose to stand with no named writer behind it.
"They go with their flocks and herds / to seek the LORD, / but they do not find Him" is one sentence running over the lines: a search that fails, then its reason. No line is set against its opposite.

"For He has torn us to pieces, / but He will heal us; / He has wounded us, / but He will bind up our wounds" plainly sets torn against heal and wounded against bind up. The call "Come, let us return to the LORD" is not part of the pairs, so the mark is cut to lines 2-5.

The second line gives a new picture and does not restate "Ephraim mixes with the nations", so "said twice" is wrong. The plain figure is the metaphor "Ephraim is an unturned cake": a people said to be a half-baked cake.

"Foreigners consume his strength, / but he does not notice. / Even his hair is streaked with gray, / but he does not know." No line is the opposite of another. Lines 1 and 3 (signs of decline) match, and so do lines 2 and 4 (he does not notice / does not know): plainly A B A' B'.
Lines 1-2 are one sentence. "They slash themselves for grain and new wine, / but turn away from Me" joins two charges and sets neither against an opposite. No form is plain at the marked words.
The "but not" sits inside line 1, and no lines are set as opposites. The plain figure is the likeness with "like" in line 2: "they are like a faulty bow".

"They set up kings, but not by Me. / They make princes, but without My approval" plainly says the same thing twice: kings/princes, not by Me/without My approval. They are not opposites, because the "but" is inside each line. The idol lines are left out.

"Though they offer sacrifices as gifts to Me, / and though they eat the meat, / the LORD does not accept them" is one sentence, and no BSB line restates another. The pairing of "remember their iniquity and punish their sins" sits inside a single line.

No line sets the opposite of another, because "but will be to them like the bread of mourners" carries the thought on. The plain figure in the marked lines is the likeness with "like": their sacrifices will be "like the bread of mourners", which defiles all who eat it.

"The days of punishment have come; / the days of retribution have arrived" plainly says the same thing twice. The mark took all seven lines, including "let Israel know it" and the closing reason, so it is cut to lines 1-2.
"He will remember their guilt; / He will punish their sins" plainly says the same thing twice. Lines 1-2 are one running sentence giving the cause, so the mark is cut to lines 3-4.

"Give them, O LORD— / what will You give?" breaks off and starts again and does not restate anything. "wombs that miscarry / and breasts that dry up" names two curses under one verb, and the second does not plainly say the first again. Too doubtful to go live.

The yoke line answers with God's act and is not plainly an opposite, so "opposite" is wrong. The plain figure is the metaphor in line 1: Ephraim is said to be "a well-trained heifer that loves to thresh".

"You have plowed wickedness and reaped injustice; / you have eaten the fruit of lies" says the harvest of sin twice. Lines 3-4 begin a new sentence that runs into 10:14, so the mark is cut to lines 1-2.
"I led them with cords of kindness, / with ropes of love" is a plain restatement. Lines 3-4 add new acts, so the mark is cut to lines 1-2.

The four "How could I..." questions plainly say the same thing again and again: give up/surrender, Ephraim/Israel, Admah/Zeboiim. "My heart is turned within Me; / My compassion is stirred!" answers the questions rather than restating them, so the mark is cut to lines 1-4.
places.span_why: "How could I give you up, O Ephraim? / How could I surrender you, O Israel?" restate each other. "make you like Admah" and "like Zeboiim" bring in a new picture of cities destroyed.

places.why: "he struggled with the angel and prevailed; / he wept and sought His favor; / he found Him at Bethel / and spoke with Him there" tells events in order, each adding something new. Nothing is restated, and "built on" would be too loose to stand without a named writer.

"and Israel worked for a wife— / for a wife he tended sheep" plainly says the same thing twice, and it shows in the BSB itself. "Jacob fled to the land of Aram" is a different act, so the mark is cut to lines 2-3. The tags on Jacob, region, Aram, served and Israel miss the words that carry the figure, so they are dropped.

"When they had pasture, / they became satisfied; / when they were satisfied, / their hearts became proud, / and as a result they forgot Me" takes up "satisfied" and climbs from pasture to pride to forgetting God. That is climbing lines, not one line said twice.
places.span_why: "they became satisfied; / when they were satisfied, / their hearts became proud" plainly takes up "satisfied" and goes a step higher. "and as a result they forgot Me" goes higher but takes up no words of the line before, so it is left out to keep fewer lines.

places.why: "Labor pains come upon him, / but he is an unwise son" sets no line against its opposite. The birth picture is there, but which form and words carry it (metaphor, alternating lines) is not plain enough to go live with no named writer.

"His fountain will fail, / and his spring will run dry" plainly says the same thing twice (fountain/spring, fail/run dry). The other six lines tell the east wind's coming and its plunder, so only lines 5-6 are marked.

"their little ones will be dashed to pieces, / and their pregnant women ripped open" names two different groups of victims, so the second line adds to the first and does not restate it. Lines 1-2 are one running sentence. Calling it "said twice" is not plain from the verse.
"I will heal their apostasy; / I will freely love them, / for My anger has turned away from them" makes two different promises and then gives the reason. No line restates another.

"his splendor will be like the olive tree, / his fragrance like the cedars of Lebanon" matches in form, but splendor and fragrance are different features, so the second line adds rather than restates. "His shoots will sprout" stands apart. "Said twice" is not plain.
Dwelling in his shade, growing grain and blossoming, and renown like the wine of Lebanon are three separate blessings. No line restates another.

"Whoever is wise, let him understand these things; / whoever is discerning, let him know them" plainly restates (wise/discerning, understand/know). Lines 3-5 are a reason and then an opposite pair (righteous walk / rebellious stumble), so they are not marked as said twice.

"Hear this, O elders; / and give ear, all who dwell in the land" plainly repeats the call to hear in other words, and you can see this in the BSB itself, not only in the original. The single tag on "give ear" (H0238) is only half of the hear/give ear pair, so the tags are dropped. Lines 3-4 are a question and are not part of the pair.

"What the devouring locust has left, / the swarming locust has eaten; / what the swarming locust has left, / the young locust has eaten..." Each pair picks up the last locust and goes one step further. These are climbing lines, not a restatement. All six lines are correctly marked.

"its teeth are the teeth of a lion, / and its fangs are the fangs of a lioness" plainly says the same thing twice (teeth/fangs, lion/lioness). "For a nation has invaded My land, / powerful and without number" does not restate, so only lines 3-4 are marked.

"The grapevine is dried up, / and the fig tree is withered" names a different tree in each line, and the list grows to "all the trees of the orchard" and then to a new point, "the joy of mankind." Each line adds; none plainly restates the one before.

"the storehouses are in ruins; / the granaries are broken down" plainly restates (storehouses/granaries, in ruins/broken down). The shriveled seeds and the closing reason are separate statements, so only lines 2-3 are marked.

"The land before them is like the Garden of Eden, / but behind them, it is like a desert wasteland" plainly sets Eden against desert. "Before them a fire devours, / and behind them a flame scorches" restates rather than opposes, and line 5 stands alone, so only lines 3-4 are marked.

"They storm the city; / they run along the wall; / they climb into houses, / entering through windows like thieves" moves step by step from city to wall to houses to windows. Each line is a new stage, so no line restates another.

"Your sons and daughters will prophesy, / your old men will dream dreams, / your young men will see visions" plainly says one thing three ways. Line 1, "I will pour out My Spirit on all people", is the cause and restates nothing, so it comes out of the span.

"they bartered a boy for a prostitute / and sold a girl for wine to drink" plainly restate each other (bartered/sold, boy/girl). "They cast lots for My people" is a different act, so it comes out of the span.

"The LORD will roar from Zion / and raise His voice from Jerusalem" is plainly said twice, and the English shows it. "heaven and earth will tremble" and the refuge lines are not part of that pair. The tags mark "roar" but not its partner "give forth his voice", and the figure does not show only in the Hebrew, so the tags come off.

No line restates another. "who dwells in Zion, My holy mountain" adds to line 1, and "Jerusalem will be holy, never again to be overrun by foreigners" is a new promise. The lines only build, which is not a plain figure. One tag falls on H1961 "it will be", which carries nothing.

"They trample on the heads of the poor / as on the dust of the earth; / they push the needy out of their way" plainly says one charge twice (poor/needy). "A man and his father have relations with the same girl..." is a separate sin, so it comes out of the span.
places.span_why: "as on the dust of the earth" only finishes the first line's picture. "They trample on the heads of the poor" is said again in "they push the needy out of their way".

places.why: The second couplet does not say the first again. It applies it to a new subject. The four lines plainly alternate: "The lion has roared" / "The Lord GOD has spoken" and "who will not fear?" / "who will not prophesy?", A B A' B'. The question is already its own place.

"but they were not satisfied" is a frustrated outcome, not a line opposed in sense. The plain figure in the marked lines is the refrain "yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.", which closes 4:6, 4:8, 4:9, 4:10 and 4:11. It is marked on those two lines only.

Plagues, the sword and the stench of the camp are separate judgments in a list. No line restates another. The plain figure in the marked lines is the refrain "yet you did not return to Me,” declares the LORD.", repeated in 4:6, 4:8, 4:9 and 4:11. It is marked on those two lines only.

"Do not seek Bethel or go to Gilgal; / do not journey to Beersheba" plainly gives one command twice. Lines 3 and 4 give the reason ("for") and do not restate lines 1 and 2, so the four lines are not one pair. The Bethel/Gilgal mirror across all four lines is already its own place.

"your transgressions are many / and your sins are numerous" plainly restates (transgressions/sins, many/numerous). The bribe lines are a second pair that names the sins and does not restate the first, so the span is trimmed to the first pair.

"but you fail to grieve over the ruin of Joseph" completes the charge against their luxury. It is not a line set against its opposite in sense. Seeing drinking and anointing as the opposite of mourning goes beyond what the verse plainly shows, and the readers disagree, so it does not go live.

"When will the New Moon be over, that we may sell grain? / When will the Sabbath end, that we may market wheat?" is a plain restatement. "Let us reduce the ephah..." is a new pair about cheating and does not restate the questions, so the span is the first four lines.

"not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, / but a famine of hearing the words of the LORD" plainly sets one famine against the other. "Behold, the days are coming... a famine on the land" is the lead-in, so it comes out of the span.

"seeking the word of the LORD, but they will not find it" is a frustrated search, not an opposite line. The plain figure is "People will stagger from sea to sea / and roam from north to east" (stagger/roam), a pair said twice, on those two lines only.

"but not a pebble will reach the ground" qualifies the sifting and is not a line answering with an opposite. The plain figure is the likeness "as grain is sifted in a sieve", which no other place marks.

"They will plant vineyards and drink their wine; / they will make gardens and eat their fruit" is a plain restatement. "I will restore My people... they will rebuild and inhabit the ruined cities" builds and restates nothing, so the span is lines 3 and 4.

places.span_why: "oh, how you will be ruined" breaks in and restates nothing, and the lines after it start a new question. The clearest pair is "If thieves came to you, / if robbers by night".

places.why: "as you drank on My holy mountain, so all the nations will drink" is a comparison, and "They will drink and gulp it down; they will be as if they had never existed" moves on to the result. No line plainly restates another.

"the house of Jacob will be a blazing fire, / and the house of Joseph a burning flame; / but the house of Esau will be stubble" plainly sets Esau against Jacob, the fuel against the fire. "Therefore no survivor will remain..." and "For the LORD has spoken" take no part in it, so the span is lines 1 to 3.
places.span_why: "the house of Joseph a burning flame" only says line 1 again, so it is not an opposite of it. The opposite is "Then the house of Jacob will be a blazing fire" against "but the house of Esau will be stubble".

places.why: "All her carved images will be smashed to pieces; / all her wages will be burned in the fire, / and I will destroy all her idols" says one thing three ways. "Since she collected the wages of a prostitute..." gives a reason and restates nothing, so the span is lines 1 to 3.
places.span_why: "All her carved images will be smashed to pieces" is plainly said again by "I will destroy all her idols". To a plain reader, "all her wages will be burned in the fire" names a different thing.

places.why: "For her wound is incurable" restates nothing. "it has reached even Judah; it has approached the gate of my people, as far as Jerusalem itself" goes a step further each time, and the readers disagree on whether it restates or builds. When in doubt it does not go live.

places.span_why: "pined for good" is set against "but calamity came down from the LORD". "even to the gate of Jerusalem" only extends the second line.

places.why: "they will cry out to the LORD, but He will not answer them" is a refused answer, not a line opposite in sense. "He will hide His face from them because of the evil they have done" continues it. The lines only build, and "hide His face" is already its own place.

"to declare to Jacob his transgression / and to Israel his sin" is a plain restating pair, and the English shows it. Lines 1 to 3 ("filled with power by the Spirit of the LORD, with justice and courage") are not part of it. The tags leave out "his sin" (H2403B) while tagging its partner, and the figure does not show only in the Hebrew, so the tags come off.

"O leaders of the house of Jacob / and rulers of the house of Israel" is a plain restating pair. "who despise justice / and pervert all that is right" is a separate pair, so the span is the first pair. The tags leave out "leaders" (H7218H) while tagging its partner "rulers", and the English shows the figure, so the tags come off.

"who build Zion with bloodshed / and Jerusalem with iniquity" is a plain restatement (Zion/Jerusalem, bloodshed/iniquity), and it shows in the English. The tags mark "bloodshed" but not its partner "injustice" (H5766B), so they misstate the pairing and come off.

"Her leaders judge for a bribe, / her priests teach for a price, / and her prophets practice divination for money" plainly says one thing three ways. "Yet they lean upon the LORD, saying..." is a new turn, so the span is lines 1 to 3.

"Zion will be plowed like a field, / Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble, / and the temple mount a wooded ridge" says one ruin three times. "Therefore, because of you" only leads in, so it comes out of the marked words. The tags run from Zion to "and Jerusalem" and leave out "heaps of ruins" and the whole temple-mount line, so they do not match the figure.

"For the law will go forth from Zion / and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem" plainly says the same thing twice. The nations' call and the teach/walk lines are not part of that pair, so the marked words narrow to lines 6 and 7. The tags fit those lines, but H3068G also lights up "LORD" in line 2, outside the figure, so they are stripped.

"the former dominion will be restored to you; / sovereignty will come to the Daughter of Jerusalem" plainly restates (dominion/sovereignty, you/Daughter of Jerusalem). The opening address is a separate pair and does not restate the promise, so the marked words narrow to lines 3 and 4. The tags include line 2's "daughter of Zion" and "to you" and leave out Jerusalem, so they are stripped.

"there you will be rescued; / there the LORD will redeem you / from the hand of your enemies!" plainly says the rescue twice. The labour likeness and the leaving for the fields and Babylon are not restated, so the marked words narrow to lines 6 to 8 (line 8 completes line 7).
places.span_why: "there you will be rescued" is said again in "there the LORD will redeem you". "from the hand of your enemies!" only completes that sentence.

places.why: "We will raise against it seven shepherds, / even eight leaders of men" restates shepherds as leaders of men, and "even" joins the two lines. "And He will be our peace" stands alone, so the marked words narrow to lines 4 and 5.

"The godly man has perished from the earth; / there is no one upright among men" plainly says one thing twice. Lines 3 and 4 are a second pair that does not restate the first, so one place cannot honestly mark all four lines as one restatement. It keeps lines 1 and 2.

"The best of them is like a brier; / the most upright is sharper than a hedge of thorns" plainly restates (best/most upright, brier/hedge of thorns). The watchmen lines are a separate pair, and "Now is the time of their confusion" adds a new point, so the marked words narrow to lines 1 and 2.

"Do not rely on a friend; / do not trust in a companion" is a plain restatement. "Seal the doors of your mouth / from her who lies in your arms" goes a step further, to one's wife, so it builds rather than restates. The marked words narrow to lines 1 and 2.

"Though I have fallen, I will arise; / though I sit in darkness, / the LORD will be my light" says the same turn twice, from fallen to rising and from darkness to light, with the two "though" clauses side by side. "Do not gloat over me, my enemy!" is an address outside the pair, so the marked words narrow to lines 2 to 4.

"He will vanquish our iniquities" is said again in "You will cast out all our sins / into the depths of the sea". Line 1, "He will again have compassion on us", does not restate it, so the span is lines 2 to 4.
places.span_why: "He will vanquish our iniquities" is said again in "You will cast out all our sins". "into the depths of the sea" adds a new picture.

places.why: "slow to anger / and great in power" adds rather than restates, and "will by no means / leave the guilty unpunished" is one clause split over two lines. The storm lines are at most a doubtful pair, since "clouds are the dust beneath His feet" adds a new picture. No plain restatement holds across the marked lines.

places.span_why: "dries it up" and "makes all the rivers run dry" restate each other. "Bashan and Carmel wither" moves to a new picture of the land, so it is a separate pair.

places.why: "Who can withstand His indignation? / Who can endure His burning anger?" plainly says the same thing twice. "His wrath is poured out like fire; / even rocks are shattered" goes on to a result, so only lines 1 and 2 are marked.

The tagged words, "the splendor of Jacob / like the splendor of Israel", are one clause making a comparison, not a line restating another. The BSB shows the same words, so "only in the original" is wrong. The pair the place would need is a different one from what its tags mark.
"The shields of his mighty men are red; / the valiant warriors are dressed in scarlet" plainly restates. The chariot and spear lines bring in new things, so only lines 1 and 2 are marked.

places.span_why: The verse holds two separate pairs. The clearer one sets "Nineveh has been like a pool of water" against "but now it is draining away". "throughout her days" only finishes the first line's sentence.
"Plunder the silver! / Plunder the gold!" restate each other. "There is no end to the treasure" is a new thought and a separate pair.

places.why: "you will go into hiding / and seek refuge from the enemy" says one act twice in other words. "You too will become drunk" is a different thought, so line 1 is left out.

places.span_why: The fire-and-sword lines and the "make yourself many" lines are two separate pairs, and "consume you like a young locust" only completes the sword line. The clearest pair is "Make yourself many like the young locust; / make yourself many like the swarming locust!".

places.why: "Your guards are like the swarming locust, / and your scribes like clouds of locusts" (with its clause "that settle on the walls") plainly restates. "When the sun rises, they fly away" goes on with the story, so lines 4 and 5 are left out.
places.span_why: "Your guards are like the swarming locust" is said again in "your scribes like clouds of locusts". "that settle on the walls on a cold day" adds a new picture.

"Why do You make me see iniquity? / Why do You tolerate wrongdoing?" plainly say the same question twice. "Destruction and violence are before me" starts a second pair that describes the scene and does not restate the questions.

places.why: "swifter than leopards, / fiercer than wolves of the night" and "Their horsemen charge ahead, / and their cavalry comes from afar" are each one thing said twice. "They fly like a vulture, / swooping down to devour" is one picture whose second line completes the first, so lines 5 and 6 are left out.
places.span_why: The horses compared with beasts and the charging horsemen are two separate pairs, and "fiercer" adds a new quality to "swifter". The clearest pair is "Their horsemen charge ahead, / and their cavalry comes from afar".

places.why: "You brandished Your bow; / You called for many arrows" plainly restates. "Selah" is not a line of the figure, and "You split the earth with rivers" is a new thought, so only lines 1 and 2 are marked.

"GOD the Lord is my strength" stands over the next lines, and "He makes my feet like those of a deer; / He makes me walk upon the heights!" goes a step further rather than plainly restating. Whether it is "same" or "building" is not plain, so it does not go live.
"I will sweep away man and beast; / I will sweep away the birds of the air, / and the fish of the sea" adds new creatures to a list rather than restating, and the span also marks "declares the LORD".

"those who bow on the rooftops / to worship the host of heaven" and "those who bow down and swear by the LORD / but also swear by Milcom" are two different groups in the list carried on from 1:4. The second does not restate the first.

"O shameful nation" is only the people addressed and does not restate line 1, so "same" is wrong. The plain figure is the verb said twice for force in "Gather yourselves, gather together" (the Hebrew has the same verb, H7197B, twice), so it is kept as doubling on those words.

"The remnant of My people will plunder them; / the remainder of My nation will dispossess them" plainly says one thing twice (remnant / remainder, My people / My nation). The span wrongly marked the oath lines and left out line 9, so it is now lines 8 and 9.

places.span_why: "She heeded no voice; / she accepted no correction" say the same thing twice. "She does not trust in the LORD; / she has not drawn near to her God" is a second pair that brings a new charge.
"Her princes are roaring lions" is said again in "her judges are evening wolves". "leaving nothing for the morning" adds to the wolves picture.

places.why: "The LORD within her is righteous; / He does no wrong" and "He applies His justice morning by morning; / He does not fail at dawn" plainly restate. "yet the unjust know no shame" is set against them, so line 5 is left out.
places.span_why: "The LORD within her is righteous; / He does no wrong" say the same thing twice. "He applies His justice morning by morning; / He does not fail at dawn" adds something new, that He is faithful every day, so it is a second pair.

places.why: "Sing for joy, O Daughter of Zion; / shout aloud, O Israel! / Be glad and rejoice with all your heart, / O Daughter of Jerusalem!" plainly restates in the BSB itself, so it is not "only in the original". The tags leave out "sing for joy" and Jerusalem and include "all" and "heart", so they do not point at the paired words.

"Do not fear, O Zion; / do not let your hands fall limp" is a plain restating pair. "On that day they will say to Jerusalem" only brings in the speech, so it is left out. The tags mark Jerusalem from that line and miss "hands fall limp", so they are dropped.

"I will save the lame / and gather the scattered" says the one rescue twice. "I will deal with all who afflict you" and "I will appoint praise and fame" are other promises, so only lines 3 and 4 are marked.

"Rejoice greatly, O Daughter of Zion! / Shout in triumph, O Daughter of Jerusalem!" plainly restates in the BSB, so it is not "only in the original". "See, your King comes to you, / righteous and victorious" does not restate, so the span is lines 1 and 2. The tags leave out "rejoice", half the pair, so they are dropped.

"These are the statutes and ordinances you must be careful to follow..." is one prose sentence with nothing going out and coming back in reverse order. The structure in the note belongs to the chapter, not this verse.

"I was glad when they said to me, / 'Let us go to the house of the LORD'" has no reversed order. The echo of "the house of the LORD" in 122:9 would be a frame, and these words mark only one end of it.
"Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good. / His loving devotion endures forever" has no reversed order. The opening "Give thanks" answered in 136:26 is a frame, and this marks only one end.
"O LORD, You have searched me / and known me" shows no reversed order. It is taken up in 139:23, "Search me, O God, and know my heart", in the same order, which would be a frame needing both verses.
"Hallelujah!" opening 149:1 and closing 149:9 is a frame, not a mirror, and this place marks all of 149:1 and nothing in 149:9.
"Hallelujah!" opening 150:1 and closing 150:6 is a frame, not a mirror, and this place marks all of 150:1 and nothing in 150:6.

The BSB sets 1 Corinthians 11:17 as one prose sentence: "In the following instructions I have no praise to offer, because your gatherings do more harm than good." Nothing in it comes back in reverse order. The search took its claim from Calvin's remark on 11:33, which is not in these words.

"And you were dead in your trespasses and sins," is one prose clause, with no lines that take turns. The past and present alternation is Bullinger's outline of the whole chapter and cannot be seen in this verse.
Colossians 2:8 is one prose sentence with no A B A' B' lines. The alternation is an outline of 2:8-23 brought in from outside the verse.

"Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus, and Timothy our brother, To Philemon our beloved fellow worker," is a plain letter greeting with nothing in reverse order. The eighteen-part introversion is Bullinger's outline of the whole letter, not something this verse shows.
